column2: A masked nocturnal bandit with a ringed tail and a suspiciously thorough habit of washing its food — and raiding bins.
The body's unmistakable signal that it wants a glass of water, not a third cup of coffee.
A tailored outer garment with sleeves and buttons — essentially a cardigan that decided to take life seriously.
The sharp defensive weapon of a bee, wasp or scorpion — tiny, yet guaranteed to ruin a picnic.
A category of art, music or literature that tells you roughly what you're signing up for before you start.
A high body temperature that has you shivering under three blankets while everyone else is in T-shirts.
A spell of unusually hot weather when the tarmac starts contemplating its liquid past.
The autumn gathering of ripe crops — the season when the fields finally settle their accounts for the year.
A tightly twisted strap used in first aid to stop serious bleeding in an emergency.
An ornamental staff held by a monarch as a symbol of royal authority — magic powers strictly optional.
A narrow trough along a roof edge or roadside designed to channel rainwater away from your shoes.
The man at the centre of a wedding, with a suit to wear and a few crucial lines to remember.
A long, slender rod of wood or metal, useful for holding up tents, flags or Olympic vaulting athletes.
A small venomous snake of southern Europe — or, to a keen angler, a predatory freshwater fish of the carp family.
The bowl-shaped mouth of a volcano, or a dramatic dent left behind by a passing meteorite.
A movement of the hands or head that conveys meaning — often louder than the words accompanying it.
A light, silvery metal used to coat steel cans — and the classic biscuit box that always turns out to hold sewing kit.
A small disc used instead of cash for arcades, trolleys or underground barriers.
The condition that separates breathing creatures from rocks — a long, unpredictable story of weekdays and wonders.
Someone who rents a flat or house and whose name eventually makes it onto the buzzer.
Buildings and shelter for people to live in — a basic necessity that comes with a remarkably long mortgage.
The tallest living land animal, effortlessly browsing leaves that nobody else in the savannah can reach.
A worker who cuts ripe grain at harvest time — or, in folklore, a cloaked figure carrying a scythe.
A professional racehorse rider for whom travelling light is literally a job requirement.
A religious minister who performs sacred rites and serves as a bridge between mortals and the divine.
A female minister of an ancient temple or pagan cult, tasked with keeping sacred traditions alive.
An insect wearing a tough, glossy shell over its wings — nature's miniature armoured car.
A professional hunter of facts, quotes and deadlines who turns the day's events into tomorrow's news.
A competition of speed where crossing the line first counts for rather more than starting well.
A untidy heap of objects — or the growing mountain of paperwork currently hiding your desk.
A solemn, binding promise or agreement that carries serious moral or legal weight.
Skin darkened by the sun — a holiday souvenir that occasionally doubles as a receipt for forgetting suncream.
The essential preparation done in advance so a big project doesn't collapse later.
Great enthusiasm and energy — or the fragrant outer peel of a lemon scraped into a cake.
High temperature, or a preliminary qualifying round in a sporting race.
A mechanical device with a strong grip used to hold things tightly together while glue dries or wheels stay put.
The daily disappearance of the sun below the horizon — a reliable light show with free admission.
A binding rule enforced by the state, breaking which tends to result in an expensive chat with a solicitor.
A large room for public gatherings, concerts or banquets, or the entrance passage inside a house.
A grand formal room in a large house where guests were historically received — and footsteps echo politely.
A simultaneous burst of gunfire or arrows, or hitting a tennis ball before it bounces.
The backward wind-up of a golf club or tennis racket just before the decisive strike.
A figure shown on a dial, meter or gauge — useful when guesswork won't quite cut it.
Working dough with the heels of your hands until it turns smooth, elastic and ready for the oven.
Soft leather with a velvety napped finish that looks magnificent right up until the first puddle.
An uncontrolled sideways slide of a car on ice or wet tarmac when the tyres stop listening to the steering wheel.
The direction where the sun goes down — reliably found on the left-hand side of a standard map.
A backup supply kept tucked away for emergencies, or a substitute player waiting on the bench.
The opening bars of a song that set the mood before the singer steps up to the microphone.
A short period of excessive indulgence, whether in food, drink or an entire television series.
A solemn promise — such as those exchanged at an altar or made privately on New Year's Day.
A stored electrical energy, a battlefield rush, or the price someone asks for their services.
A sliding metal bar that locks a door without needing a battery, an app or a password.
A clever plan or official programme — though in British English, it often sounds slightly mischievous.
A quiet, stagnant stretch of river away from the main current, or a sleepy place untouched by the rush of modern life.
A way of dealing with a problem, or the final stretch leading up to a destination.
A strategic hairstyle where remaining strands are brushed across a bald patch — brave, yet vulnerable to a brisk wind.
A successful exam result, a mountain route, or a free ticket that gets you past the security guard.
A fast, long-eared cousin of the rabbit built for sprinting across open fields.
A blazing ball of gas in deep space, or a celebrity accustomed to bright lights and entourage.
A single metal loop in a chain, or a clickable bridge taking you from one webpage to another.
A large wild animal, or a person displaying an impressive lack of manners.
A clear, ringing musical tone, most famously heard tumbling down from an English church tower.
Vibrations travelling through the air that our ears translate into speech, music or traffic.
Physical and mental well-being — a priceless asset you mostly notice the day you lose it.
An involuntary wide-mouthed intake of breath signalling boredom, tiredness or a stuffy room.
A brewed liquid with magical or medicinal powers, chiefly sold in fairy tales and fantasy novels.
Physical muscular strength — or a traditional cold terrine made from seasoned, jellied meat.
The third planet from the sun, or the dark soil beneath your boots.
The point in the sky directly overhead, or the absolute peak of someone's career.
A single tiny seed of wheat or rice, or the natural directional pattern running through timber.
The coldest season of the year, when scarves become mandatory and daylight clocks out early.
A grain crop like wheat or oats — or whatever ends up in your bowl with cold milk at seven in the morning.
Petty malice and a desire to annoy someone, rarely helpful yet remarkably persistent.
A mythical fire-breathing reptile with wings, scales and a notorious temper.
A symbol, board or gesture carrying a clear message — frequently ignored by motorists.
A long cloth strip bearing a slogan or emblem, carried at marches or draped across a high street.
An absolute blisterer of a summer day when shade becomes the best seat in town.
A shout to get someone's attention, a bird's cry, or a quick ring on the telephone.
The powdery grey residue left in the grate after a fire has burned out.
A specific area set aside for a particular purpose, such as parking, quietness or danger.
A slender surgical instrument, or an unmanned spacecraft sent to snoop around distant planets.
A folding canopy on a stick that shields you from rain — until a gust of wind turns it inside out.
A rolled dish of meat, sponge cake or pastry wrapped around a savoury or sweet filling.
The faculty of vision — the very sense currently helping you read this clue.
One of the hard white structures in your jaw that only demands attention when it starts aching.
A single tooth on the rim of a gearwheel, keeping the whole machine turning.
The European bison — a massive, shaggy woodland ox brought back from the brink of extinction.
An irritating skin sensation that insists on being scratched immediately.
A member of a major South African people, and the phonetic alphabet's word for the letter Z.
A loud, double-reeded wooden wind instrument heard at traditional celebrations across the Middle East and Balkans.
A slow, rolling rise and fall of waves on the open sea without breaking.
Ploughed farmland left unplanted for a season so the soil can catch its breath.
Your daughter's husband — the newest addition to the family table.
A graceful riverside tree with weeping branches whose timber gives us the classic cricket bat.
A slender, pointed piece of steel for sewing hems, knitting jumpers or giving injections.
A wooden crosspiece fastened over a pair of oxen, or a metaphor for heavy oppression.
A structured pastime played for fun or points — where everyone agrees to the rules until someone starts losing.
Someone taking part in a sport, board game or orchestra.
A standard of perfection worth aiming for, even if reality rarely hits the bullseye.
A blunt insult for someone acting foolishly — once a clinical term, now strictly playground and traffic vocabulary.
A carved image worshipped as a god, or a pop star worshipped by screaming teenagers.
A licensed London black cab — named after the old horse-drawn carriages once hired out for fares.
A smooth curve in a road or river where visibility drops and caution is advised.
Someone rejected by their community and left on the outside looking in.
A sharp twist in a hose or wire that stubbornly blocks the flow.
Gradual damage caused by constant use — the inevitable tax paid by favourite shoes and tyres.
A small crack or imperfection that spoils an otherwise spotless diamond or argument.
A dried grape — welcome in a fruitcake, deeply controversial when disguised as a chocolate chip in a cookie.
A sacred religious painting, a tiny clickable picture on a screen, or a cultural legend.
A sudden, involuntary spasm of the diaphragm producing an embarrassing little 'hic'.
A visual likeness, or the public reputation a celebrity works hard to polish.
A follower of Hinduism — a religious identity rather than a nationality.
A large, wattled bird that serves as the undisputed centrepiece of a British Christmas dinner.
Feathery ice crystals painted overnight across windscreens and grass when temperatures dip below freezing.
A sweet, teardrop-shaped Mediterranean fruit packed with tiny crunchy seeds.
A member of a male religious community living under vows of poverty, simplicity and prayer.
